I'll add iron-rimmed eye sockets embedded in the lid front, plus a hasp hanging from the lid center and a lock plate with a keyhole on the box front — maybe even a glowing red keyhole for character. Now I'm setting up the joint hierarchy, starting with a "body" spine joint at the box center, then figuring out how the lid functions as the upper jaw.

I'll shape the tongue as a lashing S-curve extending from the mouth, drooping down before curling upward with a raised tip, defining a sequence of points to trace its path forward and up.

For legs, I'm planning four stubby fleshy pseudopod legs with two-segment chains (hip, knee, foot) bending outward and upward, each foot ending in three claw spikes. I'm keeping them compact rather than going tentacle-style.

Reducing box lift to 0.14. For teeth, I'm planning lower teeth along the box's top rim pointing up, upper teeth along the lid's bottom rim pointing down, with larger fangs at the corners, all made from flat multi-sided cones in a yellowed bone gradient, sitting on the inner wood edge. For texturing, I'm working out a wood plank paint function: horizontal boards on the box faces, and planks that follow the curve of the dome on the lid, indexed by angle around the dome's center, with dark gaps between boards, grime near the bottom, and warm lighting toward the top.
